_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (O2C): Orders placed through the legacy Virello customer portal by strategic customers must be automatically converted into NewCo sales orders without manual re-keying during the first six months.

Verbatim from the workshop: "Some strategic customers still place orders through the legacy Virello customer portal, and the business wants those portal orders to become NewCo sales orders without manual re-keying during the first six months."

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-O2C-001 — Order-to-cash end-to-end standard flow [O2C]
Standard process: The delivered sales flow starts with a sales order that determines the customer, materials, quantities, dates, and prices. An availability check confirms whether the requested quantity can be delivered on the requested date. An outbound delivery is created, goods are picked and packed, and goods issue posts the inventory movement and the cost of goods sold. Billing creates the invoice and posts the receivable to accounting, where it is cleared when payment arrives. Each handover between these steps is delivered, and document flow links the documents so the chain is traceable in both directions.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Sales order entry with pricing, dates, and item categories.; Availability check against stock and planned receipts.; Outbound delivery, picking, packing, and goods issue.; Billing document creation and the resulting accounts receivable posting.; Document flow across the whole chain.
Common configuration points: Sales document types, item categories, and schedule line categories.; Availability checking groups and checking rules.; Delivery types, picking, and packing controls.; Billing types and copy control between documents.
Typically beyond the standard: Replacing the delivered document flow with a different chain of documents.; Creating sales orders from a payload format the standard inbound processing does not recognize.

### KB-O2C-006 — Sales order intake channels [O2C]
Standard process: Orders reach the system through several delivered channels: manual entry, released APIs, and standard inbound message processing for widely adopted electronic document formats. When the sending side is a portal, marketplace, or customer application whose payload is not one of those formats, the standard has no way to interpret it. Converting that payload into sales orders means building the receiving endpoint or the polling job, the mapping from the external structure to order fields, the determination of customer and material from external identifiers, the error handling for records that cannot be mapped, and the monitoring that tells operations what failed overnight.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Released APIs for creating and changing sales orders.; Inbound processing for standard electronic document formats.; Duplicate detection on the customer's reference number.; Incompletion procedures that hold orders until required data is present.
Common configuration points: Partner profiles and message types for electronic document exchange.; Incompletion procedures per sales document type.; Customer material info records mapping external material identifiers.
Typically beyond the standard: Converting a portal-specific payload into sales orders without manual re-entry.; Scheduled polling of an external order source and the operational surface around it.

### KB-P2P-002 — Purchase order release (approval) strategies [P2P]
Standard process: Purchasing documents can be blocked from further processing until approvers release them. The delivered release framework evaluates characteristics of the document, most commonly the total net order value, but also plant, purchasing group, document type, and account assignment category. A release strategy groups a sequence of release codes, each assigned to a role, and the strategy that applies to a given document is determined from the characteristic values. Multiple release levels with different approvers and different value limits are the normal shape of this framework, and setting them up means maintaining release groups, release codes, characteristics, classes, and strategies as customizing content. No code is involved in changing which value triggers which approver.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Multi-level release with sequential or parallel approvers.; Release determined from document characteristics including total value and currency.; Release blocks that prevent goods receipt or invoice processing until released.; Release indicator behaviour on document change, including re-triggering approval.
Common configuration points: Release groups, release codes, release indicators, and release strategies.; Characteristics and classes used to select the strategy, such as value bands.; Value limits per release level and assignment of approvers to release codes.; Whether a document change resets an already granted release.
Typically beyond the standard: Release routing that depends on an attribute not available as a delivered characteristic.; Requiring an entry in a field that the purchasing document does not deliver before release is permitted.

### KB-P2P-003 — Extending purchasing documents with custom fields and checks [P2P]
Standard process: The purchasing document carries a defined set of header and item fields. When a project needs to capture information the delivered document does not hold, the document can be extended with custom fields that are added to the persistence, the user interface, and where relevant the released APIs. Logic that must run when the document is saved, checked, or released is placed at published extension points rather than by modifying delivered code. A requirement that says a buyer must enter a reason, a justification, or a reference before a document may proceed, where the field to hold that text does not exist on the delivered document, is an extension of the standard process rather than a change to it: the release framework itself continues to work exactly as delivered.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Custom fields can be added to purchasing document header and item and surfaced on the user interface.; Extension points run at save, at check, and at release of purchasing documents.; Custom fields can be exposed on released APIs and in analytical views.
Common configuration points: Field status control over delivered purchasing fields.; Screen layout per document type and per transaction.
Typically beyond the standard: A mandatory custom text or reference field enforced before release, keyed to a business classification.; Conditional checks that depend on a material or supplier attribute the standard document does not carry.; Cross-document checks reaching into data the delivered check cannot reach.

parsed.rationale: The requirement is to automatically convert orders from a legacy portal into sales orders without manual re-keying. KB-O2C-006 states that when a sending portal uses a payload not in a standard format, 'the standard has no way to interpret it' and that 'Converting a portal-specific payload into sales orders without manual re-entry' is typically beyond the standard. KB-O2C-001 also confirms that creating sales orders from an unrecognized payload format is beyond the standard. Therefore, this requires building the receiving endpoint, mapping, error handling, and monitoring—new development.
